Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud's results for the Q2 FY2024. With me on the call are Mike Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Lena Voss, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Harlan.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud had a strong Q2, driven by continued growth in our cloud platform and increasing adoption of our AI-powered services.

During the quarter, we focused on four key areas: expanding our global infrastructure, enhancing our platform security, driving innovation in AI and machine learning, and strengthening our partnerships.

Let me elaborate on our global infrastructure expansion, which really highlights the diversification and strength of our footprint. Total revenue hit $28.7 billion, up 32% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter, powered by strong demand for our AI-optimized IaaS, PaaS, and sovereign cloud solutions. In the Americas, which made up 52% of revenue at $14.9 billion, we saw 35% YoY growth, our primary growth engine thanks to hyperscale AI workloads and enterprise migrations. U.S. public sector jumped 42% YoY, highlighted by a $2.5 billion multi-year deal with the Department of Defense for our FedRAMP High-authorized GovCloud regions, much like the momentum at AWS and Azure. Canada and Latin America, now 12% of Americas revenue, grew 28%, boosted by edge computing in our new São Paulo and Querétaro data centers for low-latency fintech apps similar to those at Nubank.

EMEA accounted for 28% of revenue, $8.0 billion, with 29% YoY growth, edging above our company average. Europe, at 22% of total revenue, benefited from GDPR-compliant data residency and the EU Data Act's emphasis on cloud portability. Germany and the UK both exceeded 35% YoY growth, with major DAX 40 automotive players scaling generative AI training in our Frankfurt region using NVIDIA H100 GPU instances, akin to Azure's OpenAI support. The Middle East and Africa added 45% YoY growth to $1.2 billion, driven by sovereign cloud in the UAE and Saudi Arabia—our Riyadh region launched last quarter, securing NEOM workloads aligned with Vision 2030.

APAC was our star performer at 20% of revenue, $5.8 billion, surging 38% YoY amid AI and 5G demand, where we're gaining on Alibaba Cloud in enterprise segments. Japan and Australia topped 40% growth via Tokyo-3 and Sydney zones for hyperscalers like SoftBank's AI projects. Greater China, 6% of total revenue, grew 25% YoY navigating regulations through hybrid multi-cloud partnerships compliant with MLPS 2.0. India and Southeast Asia exploded 55% YoY to $1.1 billion, accelerated by Mumbai-2 and Singapore expansions; a Reliance Jio-like hyperscaler shifted 20% of workloads to us, leveraging UPI fintech scale and our Graviton4 ARM instances for 25% better TCO over x86.

Key drivers include AI revenue, now 45% of total and up 65% YoY, with APAC at 75% thanks to Project Aurora's 100,000+ custom TPUs hitting 85% utilization, rivaling Google Cloud. Data sovereignty via India's DPDP Act and EU Gaia-X boosts localized edge—we invested $4.2 billion in capex for 15 new edge sites, cutting latency 40% for IoT/5G, vital for APAC telcos like Singtel on our Outposts. Customer diversification shines: top 20 grew 22%, long-tail developers on AetherStack PaaS expanded 40%, churn under 5%, net expansion at 128% from sticky SAP S/4HANA migrations in EMEA. We're tilting toward emerging markets—APAC/EMEA now 48% vs. 42% last year, aiming for 55% by FY2026 with $15 billion FY2024 capex for 20 new Availability Zones. Q3 sees Americas at 30%, APAC at 45%, full-year $115-118 billion.

Now I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Mike. As Mike highlighted, we delivered strong financial performance in Q2. Revenue grew by 32% year-over-year to $28.7 billion. Our gross margin expanded to 72%, and our operating margin reached 35%.

Before handing back, let me detail our cost optimization initiatives, which have been central to our operational excellence amid AI demands, hyperscale expansions, and macro pressures like energy costs and chip shortages. Year-to-date, we've generated over $450 million in run-rate savings, lifting adjusted EBITDA margins by 320 basis points to 38.2%—surpassing guidance and peers like Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

First, infrastructure efficiency via AetherX2 custom ARM-based processors, now in 65% of our fleet up from 40%. These ASICs offer 28% better TOPS-per-watt than Intel Xeon or AMD EPYC, cutting power use. Liquid cooling with Vertiv partners covers 45% of U.S. East and EU-West, dropping cooling OpEx 22% despite heatwaves pushing industry PUE to 1.45. This slashed data center COGS 19% sequentially to $972 million, energy costs down 15% or $180 million run-rate, faster than AWS Graviton rollout, aiding SMB/enterprise VMware migrations post-Broadcom.

Second, AI-driven optimization with AetherOptix using Kubernetes Autoscaler and Airflow-based predictive scaling from 18 months of 2.5 million instance telemetry. This automates 85% rightsizing to burstable t4g or spot instances—now 32% of compute, up from 18% YoY. Committed Use Discounts and Savings Plans hit 72% adoption via console TCO tools, above Azure's 65%. Customers saved 34% on compute, driving 14% net retention and 22% ARR growth from AI users. Internally, $210 million savings, variable compute margins to 58% despite 41% exabyte growth; GPU MIG on H100s cut idle 40% amid Hopper shortages.

Third, supply chain: multi-year NVIDIA/AMD deals for 20% off MI300X, 55% silicon from TSMC Arizona for risk mitigation, 800Gbps photonics switches from Broadcom slashing interconnect costs 18%. CapEx to 12% of revenue from 16%, freeing $120 million for R&D in AetherSecure TEEs.

Regionally: North America (72% revenue) PUE 1.18 via NextEra PPAs, $280 million savings offsetting Texas energy hikes. EMEA (18%) 48% carbon-free energy targeting 60% FY25, edge densification cut egress 26% for $85 million despite growth. APAC (10%) peering with Alibaba saved 31% transit, $85 million supporting 52% growth.

These build moats on TCO, NPS 68 up 12 points, Scope 1+2 emissions down 24% to 150g CO2e/kWh. H2 savings $300-350 million, EBITDA 39-40%; edge AI to 20% workloads, EMEA JVs. Risks GPU volatility, but diversified.

Now, I'll hand it back to Mike for further comments.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you, Sarah. We are particularly excited about the momentum we are seeing with AetherForge, our new AI platform, which is driving significant revenue acceleration and workload efficiency for our customers.

Our compute and storage utilization rates underscore this demand elasticity and efficiency. Overall compute utilization hit 87%, up 450 bps QoQ from 82.5% and 620 bps YoY from 80.8%—our highest in two years, fueled by GenAI training/inference on NexusAI clusters, sorry, AetherAI clusters. General-purpose compute at 84%, steady QoQ up 500 bps YoY via rightsizing tools optimizing 15% capacity, integrated into FinOps like AWS Compute Optimizer. Accelerators GPUs/TPUs at 95%, up 1,200 bps QoQ, with RPOs 3x YoY; throttling commitments to maintain SLAs akin to Google TPU v5p.

Storage at 91%, up 200 bps QoQ 350 bps YoY: object at 93% with 28% exabyte growth, tiering 22% to Glacier-like for 14% margin gain; block/file 87% improved by NexusFlash NVMe 2x density. Eight-quarter trend: compute from 76% post-crypto to 87%, tied to 45% AI revenue growth; storage sticky at 89% avg, every 100 bps adds $150 million EBITDA.

Regions: US 92% compute/94% storage, Virginia 96% GPUs prompting expansions. EMEA 85%/89% up 800 bps on sovereign/GDPR auto ramps. APAC 82%/88% up 1,000 bps compute on hyperscalers/5G, GPU cap at 88% but Edge unlocks 500 bps.

Our playbook: custom NexusCore Arm 35% fleet 40% perf/Watt, Spot 25% mix blending to 105%, PUE 1.18 60% renewable adding 15 GW sustainably. Q3 88-90%, Blackwell ramps; 250 bps margin FY25.

We continue to invest in research and development to stay ahead of the curve in the rapidly evolving cloud landscape. Our commitment to innovation is reflected in our recent advancements in sovereign edge computing.

On currency fluctuations, with 60%+ international revenue, FX was a headwind this quarter, but constant currency shows strength. Reported revenue $28.7 billion up 32% YoY, but FX shaved points—unfavorable JPY/EUR as noted earlier. Constant currency would be higher, aligning with 28% RPO growth to whatever fits scale. U.S. 52% insulated at 35% growth on Kubernetes/AI Nitro-like. EMEA 28% hit hardest by euro -6.2% GBP -4.8% for ~$ equivalent headwind 15% of growth, but CC 35% on sovereign. APAC yen -8.1% drag, but AUD steady; CC strong. Emerging similar.

We hedge 70-80% 12-month via forwards/options mitigating 40%, local billing in 14 currencies cuts risk—APAC yen churn down 15%. Q3 4-6% headwind, AI FX model 92% accurate. Durable demand adds $ billions AI ARR.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Thanks for taking my question. Mike, great quarter on AI—can you expand on the regional differences in AI adoption and how Project Aurora is contributing?

Mike Harlan:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, AI is 45% of revenue up 65% YoY, APAC leading at 75% with Aurora's TPUs at 85% util across new sovereign sites. Americas hyperscale public sector like DoD deal ramps training, EMEA autos in Frankfurt H100s, APAC SoftBank/India hyperscalers on Graviton4. Aurora directly competes with Google TPUs, deploying 100k+ units fueling that regional mix shift to 48% APAC/EMEA. Happy to follow up.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Hi team, on the cost optimizations—$450 million YTD is impressive. How sustainable are these as AI capex ramps, and any regional variances?

Sarah Chen:
Lisa, great question. These are structural, not one-offs—custom silicon to 65% fleet, AI rightsizing at 85% automation, supply hedges locking 20% GPU discounts. Sustainability from PUE 1.18, renewables 60%, turning savings into R&D moats like TEEs. Regional: NA highest ROI $280M, EMEA $85M despite energy, APAC $85M on peering. H2 another $300-350M, margins to 39-40% even as AI scales. Sustainable edge over hyperscalers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Lena, with compute util at 87% and GPUs 95%, are you seeing constraints? How's the tech roadmap addressing supply for Blackwell equivalents?

Dr. Lena Voss:
Raj, thanks for the question. Yes, 95% GPU util reflects insatiable GenAI demand—we're throttling select zones like Google did with TPUs, but our multi-vendor strategy TSMC/Intel Foundry derisks Blackwell ramps Q4. Roadmap: NexusAccel GPUs optimized for Llama-scale, MIG partitioning cuts idle 40%, Capacity Blocks for AI reservations like AWS. Custom Arm NexusCore at 35% general compute boosts perf/Watt 40%. Adding 15GW sustainably at 1.18 PUE. No major constraints, positioned for 88-90% Q3.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi, Sarah or Mike—FX was a drag, any update on Q3 guidance incorporating that, and full-year constant currency outlook?

Mike Harlan:
Emily, Sarah covered the hedges mitigating 40%, local billing stabilizing. Q3 FX 4-6% headwind at spot, but CC growth accelerates APAC to 45%, Americas 30%, full-year $115-118B holds firm CC 28-30% like RPO. AI ARR net new scales it, derisked by multi-region data gravity. Confident.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you for your questions and your continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
